title: 高市早苗首相が初の訪米　米国の待遇や歴代首相との違いは？
extracted_text:
米国の外交上最も格式が高い接遇は国賓で、大統領や国王ら元首級が対象だ。内閣の長である日本の首相もこれに準じた「国賓待遇」にする例がある。通常の公式訪問などと一線を画し、手厚い儀礼でもてなして友好関係を強調する。今回は国賓待遇と銘打っていないものの、夕食会があるなど厚遇といえる。

国賓待遇の場合はホワイトハウスでの歓迎式典に始まり、首脳会談の後に共同記者会見が設けられることが多い。今回は共同記者会見は実施しない見通しだ。宿泊先は一般にホワイトハウスの近くの大統領迎賓館「ブレアハウス」になる。

日本の首相が米国を公式訪問した近年の主な例には15年の安倍晋三氏、24年の岸田文雄氏が挙げられる。いずれも米議会での演説に臨んだ。高市首相は国会答弁で、米側から議会演説の打診を受けたものの日程上の理由で見送ったと説明した。

米国は日本にとって「外交の基軸」とも呼ぶ同盟国だ。日本の歴代首相は就任すると早期訪米の機会を探ってきた。首脳間の関係を早い段階で深め、日米関係の重要性を確認する場として位置づけてきた。

今回の高市首相は25年10月の首相就任からおよそ5カ月で訪米が実現した。訪米は近年の首相の中で際立って早くはないものの、首相の就任直後にトランプ氏を日本に迎えている。半年もたたずに相互訪問が実現するのは珍しい。

石破茂前首相は就任から4カ月だった。日米の懸案として米関税交渉が重要になる状況で、対米投資を1兆ドルにすると打ち出し、関係づくりに力を注いだ。

新型コロナウイルス禍の影響があった岸田氏は1年3カ月、菅義偉氏は7カ月だった。菅氏は当時のバイデン大統領との共同声明で「台湾海峡の平和と安定」という文言を明記した。

今回の訪米は米国とイスラエルによるイラン攻撃後、最初の日米首脳会談になる。首相が日本の姿勢をどう打ち出し、トランプ氏が何を日本に期待するのかが焦点になる。

米国の新たな関税措置や日本の対米投資案件の公表にも関心が集まる。当初はトランプ氏の訪中を前に日米が対中国への考え方を擦り合わせる機会としても想定していた。対中認識を巡るやり取りも重要になる。

高市首相は安倍首相時代の「蜜月関係」を引き継ぎ、トランプ氏との良好なつながりづくりに努めてきた。両首脳は25年10月の日本での初顔合わせから、互いに「ドナルド」「サナエ」と呼びあって親密さを発信した。

首相は「日米同盟の新たな黄金時代をつくりたい」と呼びかけた。米側によるとトランプ氏をノーベル平和賞に推薦する意向も示した。トランプ氏は「彼女とは非常に良い関係を築いている」と強調した。

衆院選の際は選挙戦終盤にトランプ氏が首相と自民党、日本維新の会の連立政権についてSNSで支持を打ち出した。「米大統領として完全かつ全面的に支持する」と投稿した。米大統領が日本の国政選挙で与党への支持を明らかにするのは異例だ。

トランプ氏は衆院選後の2月16日、自民党の圧勝に関し首相が「私の支持を要因に挙げていた」と一方的に主張した。首相は9日、X（旧ツイッター）上で「トランプ大統領の温かいお言葉に心から感謝いたします」と謝意を示していた。

日本の首相はこれまでも同盟国の最高権力者である米大統領との個人的な関係に腐心してきた。安倍氏は16年の大統領選でトランプ氏が当選すると、大統領就任前にニューヨークのトランプタワーを訪れて面会した。

歴代首相がワシントンを訪れる際にも友好関係を演出してきた。高市首相とトランプ氏が今回どのように関係性を象徴する場をつくるかも注目ポイントだ。

translated_text:
The highest level of diplomatic protocol in US diplomacy is a state visit, reserved for heads of state such as presidents and kings. Japan's prime minister, as the head of the cabinet, has also occasionally received equivalent "state visit treatment." This sets it apart from regular official visits, emphasizing the friendly relationship through generous ceremonies. Although this time it wasn't labeled as a state visit, the generous treatment, including a dinner party, can be considered special treatment.

In cases of state visit treatment, it typically begins with a welcoming ceremony at the White House, followed by a joint press conference after the summit talks. This time, a joint press conference is not expected to be held. The accommodation is generally at the Blair House, the official guest residence for the president near the White House.

Recent examples of Japanese prime ministers making official visits to the US include Shinzo Abe in 2015 and Fumio Kishida in 2024. Both delivered speeches at the US Congress. Prime Minister Takaichi explained in a Diet response that she was invited by the US side to give a congressional speech, but she declined due to scheduling reasons.

The US is an ally that can be called the "pillar" of Japan's diplomacy. Japanese prime ministers have generally sought opportunities for early visits to the US after taking office. They have viewed early summits as an opportunity to deepen relations between leaders at an early stage and confirm the importance of the Japan-US alliance.


This visit by Prime Minister Takaichi was realized approximately five months after she took office in October 2025. While the visit is not unusually early compared to recent prime ministers, she welcomed Trump to Japan right after taking office. It is rare for mutual visits to occur within half a year.

Former Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba visited the US four months after taking office. With US tariff negotiations being an important issue between Japan and the US, he announced plans to increase investment in the US to $1 trillion, focusing on building relationships.

Prime Minister Kishida, affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, visited after one year and three months, while Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga visited after seven months. Suga, in a joint statement with President Biden at the time, included language regarding "peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait."

This visit will be the first Japan-US summit since the US and Israel's attack on Iran. How the prime minister presents Japan's position and what Trump expects from Japan will be focal points.


There is also keen interest in the US's new tariff measures and announcements of Japanese investment projects in the US. Initially, it was also seen as an opportunity for Japan and the US to align their approach toward China ahead of Trump's visit to China. Exchanges regarding views on China will also be important.


Prime Minister Takaichi has carried forward the "close relationship" from the Abe administration and has worked to build a good rapport with Trump. Since their first meeting in Japan in October 2025, both leaders have addressed each other by their first names, Donald and Sanae, projecting intimacy.


The prime minister has called for "creating a new golden era of the Japan-US alliance." According to the US side, they also expressed intent to nominate Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize. Trump emphasized that he has "a very good relationship with her."

During the lower house election, Trump expressed support on social media for the coalition government of the prime minister, the LDP, and Nippon Ishin at the final stage of the campaign. He posted that "as US president, I give complete and full support." It is unusual for a US president to openly express support for a Japanese political party in a national election.

On February 16 after the lower house election, Trump unilaterally claimed that the LDP's landslide victory was due to his support. On the 9th, the prime minister had expressed gratitude on X (formerly Twitter), saying "I am sincerely grateful for President Trump's warm words."

Japanese prime ministers have also always devoted careful attention to building personal relationships with US presidents, who are the supreme authority in allied nations. When Trump was elected in the 2016 presidential election, Abe visited Trump Tower in New York to meet with him before he took office.


Previous prime ministers have also staged friendly relationships when visiting Washington. How Prime Minister Takaichi and Trump will create a symbolic moment for their relationship this time is also a point of interest.
